description: The provided image is a radial, multi-layered pie chart illustrating the structure of medical ethics principles as they relate to the MedEthicsQA benchmark, which evaluates large language models (LLMs) on medical ethics. At the center, the core principle “Beneficence” is represented by a large teal segment, from which numerous sub-principles radiate outward, including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” and “Ethical Research.” Adjacent to Beneficence are three other major ethical pillars: “Justice” (in reddish-brown), encompassing “Promote the Health of Community,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally”; “Non-Maleficence” (in purple), including “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain”; and “Autonomy” (in green), covering “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed,” “Keep Confidential,” and “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve.” Each principle and sub-principle is clearly labeled within its colored segment, and the chart visually organizes ethical domains hierarchically, with Beneficence occupying the largest central area, suggesting its foundational role in the framework. The overall design emphasizes the interconnectedness and relative scope of each ethical category within the benchmark’s evaluation structure.
